Power by simulation

Source: R/pwrsim.R
pwrsim.Rd

The power of a two-arm trial found by simulating it: for each control arm size in n and each effect in eff, nsim trials are drawn, each is tested, and the power is the share rejected at alpha, with its Monte Carlo standard error and Wilson's interval (Morris, White and Crowther 2019). It answers what a formula cannot: an outcome that is binary or a count, unequal arms, a permutation test.

Usage

pwrsim(
  n,
  eff,
  fam = c("normal", "binary", "poisson"),
  sd = 1,
  p0 = 0.5,
  mu0 = 1,
  ratio = 1,
  test = c("welch", "perm"),
  alt = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  nsim = 1000,
  nperm = 199,
  level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'pwrsim'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

n

The control arm sizes to try: whole numbers from 2 to 1000000.

eff

The effects to try: differences in means (in the outcome's units; risk differences for "binary").

fam

The outcome: "normal", "binary" or "poisson".

sd

The standard deviation of a normal outcome: positive.

p0

The control arm's chance of a binary outcome, from 0 to 1; p0 + eff must be too.

mu0

The control arm's mean of a Poisson outcome: positive; mu0 + eff must be at least 0.

ratio

The treated arm's size over the control arm's: positive.

test

"welch" or "perm".

alt

The alternative: "two.sided", "greater" (the treated higher) or "less".

alpha

The level of the test: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

nsim

The trials drawn per design: a whole number from 1 to 1000000.

nperm

The relabellings of the permutation test: a whole number from 1 to 100000 with 1 / (nperm + 1) at most alpha.

level

The level of Wilson's interval: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

seed

NULL (drawn from R's generator, so set.seed() fixes it) or a whole number from 0 to 2147483647.

x

An object of class pwrsim.

...

Not used by print().

Value

An object of class pwrsim, a list: tab, a data frame with one row per design (n varying fastest): n, n1 (the treated arm), eff, power, se, lo, hi and rej (the trials rejected); and fam, test, alt, alpha, nsim and seed.

Details

The control arm has n units and the treated arm round(ratio * n). The outcome is normal with standard deviation sd and mean 0 in the control arm and eff in the treated arm (fam = "normal"), 0 or 1 with chance p0 and p0 + eff ("binary"), or Poisson with mean mu0 and mu0 + eff ("poisson"), drawn by inversion from the package's generator. The test is Welch's t test (test = "welch"; with no spread in either arm the p-value is 0 when the means differ in the direction tested, else 1) or the permutation test of the difference in means with nperm relabellings ("perm"; p = (1 + k) / (1 + nperm)). Each design has a stream of its own made from seed and its place in the grid, so a design's power does not depend on the others.

References

Morris, T. P., White, I. R. and Crowther, M. J. (2019). Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods. Statistics in Medicine, 38(11), 2074-2102. doi:10.1002/sim.8086

Welch, B. L. (1947). The generalization of 'Student's' problem when several different population variances are involved. Biometrika, 34(1-2), 28-35. doi:10.1093/biomet/34.1-2.28

Wilson, E. B. (1927). Probable inference, the law of succession, and statistical inference. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 22(158), 209-212. doi:10.1080/01621459.1927.10502953

Examples

pwrsim(c(20, 50), eff = c(0, 0.5), nsim = 400, seed = 1)
#> pwrsim: normal outcome, welch test (two.sided) at alpha 0.05, 400 trials per design
#>   n n1 eff  power          se         lo         hi rej
#>  20 20 0.0 0.0375 0.009499178 0.02285503 0.06094384  15
#>  50 50 0.0 0.0350 0.009188988 0.02096129 0.05788514  14
#>  20 20 0.5 0.3425 0.023727292 0.29769102 0.39030535 137
#>  50 50 0.5 0.6925 0.023072914 0.64562516 0.73571260 277
pwrsim(100, eff = 0.15, fam = "binary", p0 = 0.3, nsim = 400,
       seed = 2)$tab
#>     n  n1  eff power        se       lo        hi rej
#> 1 100 100 0.15 0.585 0.0246361 0.536129 0.6322539 234
